extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural researchers, grant applicants, institutional research administrators, and other stakeholders in NIH grants
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy updates, resources, and procedural changes relevant to preparing and submitting NIH grant applications. Items signal requirements, new formats, review-process changes, and initiatives applicants should know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose scientifically sound experimental/models (including NAMs) that are appropriate to the specific research question; prioritize human relevance/translational potential where appropriate. The blurb functions as evaluative guidance: model choice should be justified by fit to the research question and translational aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — application format and linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants to PF5 should use the specified application format, understand the PF5 award structure, and be aware that applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time (JIT). The item advises using the NIH overview video to learn these procedural/format expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format — 2026 Pilot
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans (pilot format), follow the 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format and its simplified required elements. This is a prescriptive format requirement — applicants should use the new template/structure when submitting DMS Plans as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and reproducibility expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should embed replication and reproducibility considerations throughout applications and awards. The Initiative and Gold Standard Science plan indicate NIH will encourage, incentivize, and possibly expect concrete plans or practices that promote reproducibility and replication (e.g., study design, preregistration, replication experiments, transparent methods/data).

rubrics_metrics.name: "Competitive but not discussed" (CBND) review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes a procedural scoring outcome from emergency review modifications: applications in the middle third of a study section can be labeled 'competitive but not discussed' and thus not discussed in full review even if strong. Applicants should understand this possible outcome and its implications for being discussed and for next steps (e.g., JIT, resubmission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized peer review (CSR consolidation) — implications for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: "In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) ... providing an update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that peer review consolidation within CSR may affect review assignment, timing, and processes. The stated goals are increased efficiency, competition, and transparency; applicants may need to monitor how centralization changes review expectations or procedures.
